The aggregate cell metadata records actual parallel use, five subagents, a failed solution, and 518/887 passed tests.
The completed official status records mode parallel, protocol success, evaluation completion, and failed solution_passed false.

The final answer says the replacement is in src/executable.py, compile.sh installs it, and smoke checks passed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-level trajectory wrapper for the parallel run; no semantic events were projected from this source.

The parallel parent split docs and CLI probing to children, probed and implemented locally, spawned template mapping, built src/executable.py, observed a child build-path overwrite, repaired compile.sh, and closed after final smoke checks.
The doc_reader child accumulated docs and probes, then independently wrote src/crowbook.py, rewrote compile.sh to install it as ./executable, ran the new build, and was later aborted.
The probe_cli child exercised the binary across options, templates, ODT, config, and error behavior, returned findings, and was then interrupted by the parent.
A nested child under doc_reader performed additional CLI and output probing, including HTML, EPUB, PDF, and ODT observations, then returned a concise findings summary.
The template_mapper child captured template-related behavior, option names, and variable syntax, then returned implementation guidance for lightweight template handling.

direct_file_reviews.summary: The prompt is the same clean-room reverse-engineering task and forbids source retrieval, wrapping, or binary analysis.
The aggregate cell metadata records serial mode, no subagents, failed solution_passed false, and 572/887 passed tests.
The completed official status records zero spawn calls, no parallel use, evaluator completion, and failed solution_passed false.
The evaluation summary confirms the official ProgramBench evaluator completed with 572 passed and 315 failed tests.
The final answer says crowbook_cleanroom.py was installed through compile.sh as ./executable and smoke-tested broadly.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-level trajectory wrapper for the serial run; no semantic events were projected from this source.

The serial actor read docs, probed the binary through CLI behavior, tried a Rust scaffold, pivoted to a dependency-free Python script, installed it as ./executable, compared against observed outputs, and completed final smoke checks.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the clean-room Crowbook CLI task, including docs, config files, single markdown mode, help/version, templates, stats, and output formats.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split observation work to doc_reader and probe_cli, later spawned template_mapper, and also kept local implementation ownership, but deliverable ownership was not exclusive because a child produced its own executable path.
parallel.implementation: The parent first attempted Rust, abandoned it after offline dependency failure, then wrote a pure Python src/executable.py. A child also wrote src/crowbook.py with overlapping CLI/rendering behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent intended compile.sh to install src/executable.py, but a child rewrote compile.sh to copy src/crowbook.py into ./executable, requiring late parent reconciliation.
parallel.verification: The parent ran py_compile, source-level behavior checks, final build checks, stats checks, and HTML smoke tests on the rebuilt executable after restoring compile.sh.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final official score remained failed at 518/887. The trajectory shows a late build-path collision and repair, plus ordinary incompleteness in the Crowbook reimplementation.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room Crowbook task and covered CLI options, create, list-options, templates, book config, single-file mode, output formats, stats, quiet mode, and error behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, build, verification, and final delivery, with no child agents or competing workspace owners.
serial.implementation: The actor tried a Rust scaffold, found the offline dependency path blocked, pivoted to a dependency-free Python crowbook_cleanroom.py, and iteratively patched mismatches.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The actor moved the original binary aside for comparison, used compile.sh to install crowbook_cleanroom.py as ./executable, and kept one active final build path.
serial.verification: The serial run compared help/version, create, list-options, templates, HTML, EPUB, TeX/PDF/html.dir behavior, --set handling, missing-file cases, and then smoke-tested the built artifact.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final official score still failed at 572/887, so the implementation was incomplete even though it was more coherent and better-scoring than the parallel attempt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room reimplementation task and claimed coverage of help/version, parse errors, list-options, templates, create, stats, HTML/EPUB/TEX, localization, and some failure modes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task and claimed coverage of help/version, create, list-options, templates, .book and --single HTML, EPUB, TeX, stats, quiet mode, and error paths.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the task, but serial covered a somewhat broader and more orderly observed surface while parallel lost time stabilizing which implementation was actually delivered.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated docs and CLI probing to children, later added template mapping, while the parent also kept a local implementation track.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation or child activity and kept probing, implementation, build, and delivery in one thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent probing but lacked exclusive ownership over the submitted build path, whereas serial had a single accountable owner for all stages.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children returned useful findings, but implementation/build ownership boundaries were loose enough for a child to create a separate entry source and rewire compile.sh.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need cross-agent interfaces; findings, implementation state, and build decisions remained in one actor's context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface gap was not a missing fact about Crowbook behavior, but a missing build-target boundary between parent and child implementation work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel abandoned Rust after cargo could not fetch crates, wrote src/executable.py, then had to compare that implementation against a child's separate src/crowbook.py path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also abandoned Rust after offline dependency failure, then consolidated on crowbook_cleanroom.py and iteratively patched it against observed behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both pivoted to Python, but serial stayed on one implementation path while parallel had two overlapping scripts and needed late reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited on children, interrupted probe_cli after timeouts, consumed some returned findings, and later dealt with a child side effect in the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and no joins; all observations and decisions stayed local to one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel carried child-management overhead and late child side effects; serial avoided lifecycle joins entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child wrote src/crowbook.py, rewrote compile.sh, and installed ./executable from that source after the parent had created a different build path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed one clean-room file through compile.sh as ./executable and then verified that artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-workspace collision on the submitted build path; serial had a linear final tree with no competing writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did final smoke checks after restoring compile.sh, including asserting the installed executable matched src/executable.py and running stats and HTML output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did a final smoke pass on the built artifact itself, including version, help, and sample rendering.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified locally, but parallel's checks followed a late build-target repair and were narrower than serial's broader final verification list.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents, 782 tool calls, and 33.6M total tokens, then closed after repairing the final build path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 247 tool calls, and 15.4M total tokens, then closed after direct final smoke checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more coordination and tool budget, but the retained taxonomy issue is the concrete deliverable overwrite rather than token use alone.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations show both solutions failed, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome to explain. The serial run nevertheless materially outscored the parallel run, 572/887 versus 518/887. The best evidenced comparative contributor is that the serial run maintained a single final implementation and build path, while the parallel run had a child overwrite the build target with a separate implementation and forced the parent into late reconciliation before final smoke testing.
parallel_contributors: The child rewrote compile.sh to install src/crowbook.py and regenerated ./executable while the parent owned a different src/executable.py build path.
The parent detected the workspace had changed under its verification and had to inspect and restore compile.sh before closing.
serial_contributors: The serial actor used a single implementation file and build script path without cross-agent deliverable ownership conflict.
The serial actor performed a final smoke pass directly on the built ./executable after installation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs remained incomplete Crowbook reimplementations under the hidden evaluator.
The serial final verification list was broader, including explicit and implicit EPUB/TeX/PDF/html.dir paths, --set, and missing-file cases.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributor to quality gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a pass/fail discordance

candidates.reason: Implementation was actively owned by the parent and also attempted by a child; the problem was competing ownership, not no implementation owner.
The parent inspected the competing child implementation and reconciled compile.sh, so integration was not unowned.
Assembly of ./executable was owned by both parent and child at different points; the observed failure mode is a build-target collision.
The parent drove implementation, build, smoke testing, and final delivery, so the end-to-end pipeline was not ownerless.
The parent and children probed and implemented concurrently; productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight.
Parallel investigation overlapped with local implementation work and returned usable findings; the main adverse event was the later deliverable collision.
Although coordination was expensive, the parent still implemented and verified the final path; the directly evidenced boundary is the deliverable overwrite.
High token and tool use are present, but there is no concrete collective fan-out exhaustion that prevented a required stage from occurring.
The child wrote and built a complete competing script; the adverse consequence was not an oversized unfinished child scope but a conflicting deliverable write.
No specific known task or acceptance requirement omitted from a child brief is shown to make the work unusable; the visible harm is build ownership conflict.
There was likely no clear file/build ownership contract, but the realized event was an actual rewrite of compile.sh and ./executable, which the taxonomy ranks as a write label.
No known finding is shown to disappear through transfer and cause repeated work; the parent did receive and use child findings.
Child reports were not shown to be too large or unstructured for decision-making; the parent acted on concrete observations and inspected the competing script.
No parent action is based on a handoff describing a superseded requirement or workspace state; the parent observed the live changed workspace directly.
The conflict was not incompatible reports left unadjudicated; it was concrete concurrent modification of the submitted build path.
The parent ran final build and smoke checks after repairing the build path; hidden evaluator failure alone cannot establish unsupported completion.
There is no replacement or retry agent that repeats prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints or confirmed findings.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent interrupted probe_cli after a wait timeout, but the retained consequence is not missing probe_cli work; later final harm centers on the build-path overwrite.
A directly promotable child candidate was not simply left unpromoted; the child actually promoted its own build path and the parent later replaced it.
The parent performed final verification after restoring compile.sh, so the final accepted path was not an unverified post-check merge.
The child implementation was visible and inspected by the parent, which deliberately reverted the build path rather than failing to retrieve it.
No verifier child with a concrete trapped finding is evidenced; the child activities were probing or implementation, not an unreturned verifier result.
The parent did take over the final build path after detecting the child-induced mismatch, so there is no unrecovered child failure chain.
The parent did not ignore the competing child result; it inspected the child-created src/crowbook.py and compile.sh change before deciding.
The parent had wait timeouts, but it listed agents, interrupted one child, and later inspected workspace changes; no separate blind-wait consequence is distinct from the write conflict.
Separate implementation paths existed, but the stronger observed event is replacement of the executable/build target, so write precedence selects Deliverable Overwrite.
Both actors edited compile.sh, but the consequential collision was not merely same-file reconciliation; it changed which source became ./executable.
The overwritten path was the submitted build/executable route rather than only a non-entry source or configuration module.

A child rewrote compile.sh to copy src/crowbook.py into ./executable and ran that build path while the parent had created and was verifying src/executable.py as the intended deliverable. The parent later detected the changed workspace, inspected the child path, identified a stats mismatch, and restored compile.sh. Corrective boundary: give exactly one actor ownership of compile.sh and ./executable, or require children to return patches rather than installing submitted artifacts directly.
candidates.realized_consequence: The submitted build path was temporarily redirected to the child's different implementation, forcing the parent to spend the closing phase diagnosing the mismatch and rewriting compile.sh before final smoke tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: Source Overwrite is lower precedence because the contested object was the build/install path for the submitted executable, not only a non-entry source file.

candidates.reason: The evidence shows a targeted compile.sh and executable replacement, not a broad cleanup or promotion that replaced multiple final-tree outputs.
The workspace was shared, but a more specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven, so the catch-all shared-workspace label does not apply.
No generated artifact or temporary output from one concurrent actor was consumed as stable reference input by another actor in a contaminating way.

retained_patterns.reason: The child changed compile.sh so the submitted executable would be generated from src/crowbook.py, then ran that build, while the parent had its own src/executable.py build path. The parent later found compile.sh and ./executable no longer matched its verified source and restored the path. Corrective boundary: keep compile.sh and ./executable under one owner or require child patches to be joined before installation.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The submitted build path was temporarily redirected to the child's different implementation, forcing the parent to spend the closing phase diagnosing the mismatch and rewriting compile.sh before final smoke tests.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Source Overwrite is lower precedence because the contested object was the build/install path for the submitted executable, not only a non-entry source file.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Rejected Cross-File Scope Collision, Same-File Collision, Source Overwrite, and Unisolated Workspace Writes as lower-precedence views of the same compile.sh and ./executable collision.
Rejected Blind Timeout Wait and Early Child Termination as separate labels because the wait/interruption chain did not have a distinct final consequence from the later write conflict.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only Deliverable Overwrite had a concrete independent adverse episode with two-sided anchors.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No additional labels were retained for ordinary implementation incompleteness, hidden evaluator failures, high token use, or downstream symptoms of the same deliverable-write episode.
